statement: The function returns a result r and r equals the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) such that there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) and nums[j] < nums[i], and there exists k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] > nums[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and 0 <= r <= len(nums) - 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exist indices p and q with 0 <= p < len(nums) and 0 <= q < len(nums) and nums[p] != nums[q], then r <= len(nums) - 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let mn be the minimum of the set of values {nums[t] | 0 <= t < len(nums)} and mx be the maximum of that set. If mn < mx, then the function returns a result r and r = len(nums) - (the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = mn) - (the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = mx).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r > 0 if and only if there exist indices a, b, and c with 0 <= a < len(nums), 0 <= b < len(nums), and 0 <= c < len(nums) such that nums[a] < nums[b] < nums[c].
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = len(nums) - 2.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000, len(nums) >= 2, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) - 1, nums[i] < nums[i+1].

statement: For every slice b of 64-bit integers with len(b) = len(nums) and all entries in [-100000, 100000], if b has the same multiset of values as nums (that is, for every integer v, the number of indices i with nums[i] = v equals the number of indices j with b[j] = v), then the function returns a result r for nums and a result r_b for b, and r = r_b.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let mn be the minimum of the set of values {nums[t] | 0 <= t < len(nums)} and mx be the maximum of that set. For every integer v such that v = mn or v = mx, let nums2 be the slice of length len(nums) + 1 with nums2[i] = nums[i] for 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums2[len(nums)] = v. Then the function returns a result r for nums and a result r2 for nums2, and r2 = r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 99 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let mn be the minimum of the set of values {nums[t] | 0 <= t < len(nums)} and mx be the maximum of that set. For every integer v with mn < v < mx, let nums2 be the slice of length len(nums) + 1 with nums2[i] = nums[i] for 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums2[len(nums)] = v. Then the function returns a result r for nums and a result r2 for nums2, and r2 = r + 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 99 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.

statement: Let nums2 be the slice of length 2 * len(nums) with nums2[i] = nums[i] for 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums2[i] = nums[i - len(nums)] for len(nums) <= i < 2 * len(nums). Then the function returns a result r for nums and a result r2 for nums2, and r2 = 2 * r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 50 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000.
